title: Face decomposition of cofibrant finite-subset diagrams
statement:
Use small simplicial sets of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] and ordinary small colimits of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], formed degreewise in sets. For a finite set $T$, write $\mathcal P_{<}(T)$ for the category of its proper subsets, including the empty subset when proper, with a unique arrow $R\to R'$ for each inclusion. Let $S$ be a nonempty finite set, $s\in S$, $S'=S\setminus\{s\}$, and $Z:\mathcal P_{<}(S)\to\mathrm{sSet}$ a diagram. Put $A_R=Z_R$ and $B_R=Z_{R\cup\{s\}}$ for $R\subsetneq S'$, so that both are diagrams on $\mathcal P_{<}(S')$, and put $C=Z_{S'}$. The structure maps induce a natural isomorphism $C\amalg_{\operatorname{colim}A}\operatorname{colim}B\cong\operatorname{colim}Z$, where the span maps are the canonical maps $\operatorname{colim}A\to C$ and $\operatorname{colim}A\to\operatorname{colim}B$.
Suppose $Z$ is cofibrant in the explicit sense that for every proper $T\subset S$ its latching map $\operatorname{colim}_{R\subsetneq T}Z_R\to Z_T$ is degreewise injective. Then $A$ and $B$ are cofibrant in this same sense, and the maps $\operatorname{colim}A\to C$, $\operatorname{colim}A\to\operatorname{colim}B$, and $\operatorname{colim}B\to\operatorname{colim}Z$ are degreewise injective. All comparisons are natural in $Z$. The case $|S|=1$ is included, with $A$ and $B$ empty diagrams.

source.place: Section 6.3 and Proposition 6.4, printed pp. 11-12, specialized to simplicial sets; cofibrancy of the shifted face restriction and monicity of Acol to Bcol follow from the same latching induction. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this finite simplicial diagram lemma.

proof.text: First ignore cofibrancy and put $a=\operatorname{colim}A$, $b=\operatorname{colim}B$. A cocone from $Z$ to any simplicial set $M$ restricts to maps $c:C\to M$ and $v:b\to M$ agreeing on $a$. Conversely, such a pair defines the component at $S\supsetneq U$ by $c\circ Z(U\subseteq S')$ if $s\notin U$, and by $v\circ\iota_{U\setminus\{s\}}$ if $s\in U$. Here $S'=S\setminus\{s\}$, as in the statement. For an arrow crossing from $s\notin U$ to $s\in V$, one has $U\subseteq V\setminus\{s\}\subsetneq S'$; factor the arrow through $U\cup\{s\}$ and use agreement on $a$ and the $B$-cocone relation. Arrows in a single face satisfy the cocone relation already; there are no arrows from the containing face back to the non-containing face. These constructions are inverse, so the universal property gives the specified isomorphism $C\amalg_a b\cong\operatorname{colim}Z$.

source.place: Section 6.3 and Proposition 6.4, printed pp.11-12: pushout square; cocone correspondence expanded.

proof.text: We now prove the finite latching induction needed for the injectivity assertions, before applying it to either face. For a diagram $F:J\to\mathrm{sSet}$ on a finite poset, write $L_qF=\operatorname{colim}_{r<q}F_r$, and assume all maps $L_qF\to F_q$ are degreewise injective. A subset $I\subseteq J$ is downward closed if $q\in I$ and $r\leq q$ imply $r\in I$. For downward closed $I\subseteq H\subseteq J$ we prove that $\operatorname{colim}_I F\to\operatorname{colim}_H F$ is degreewise injective, by induction on $|H\setminus I|$. At zero it is the identity. At a positive value choose a minimal $q\in H\setminus I$; finiteness gives such a $q$, every $r<q$ lies in $I$, and $I^+=I\cup\{q\}$ is downward closed.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 6.4, printed p.12: explicit induction setup on finite downsets; agent expansion of the indicated finite induction.

proof.text: In this induction, $\operatorname{colim}_{I^+}F$ is the pushout $(\operatorname{colim}_I F)\amalg_{L_qF}F_q$. Indeed a cocone on $I^+$ is exactly a cocone on $I$ and a map $F_q\to M$ agreeing on every $F_r$ for $r<q$, equivalently agreeing on $L_qF$. These are all the conditions: no arrow leaves $q$ for an object of $I$, since downward closure of $I$ would then imply $q\in I$. This proves the pushout assertion from the colimit definition, without assuming any structure map $F_r\to F_q$ separately injective.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 6.4, printed p.12: one-object latching attachment, with its full cocone verification.

proof.text: Compute the attachment pushout degreewise. Apply [lem-coef-set-pushout-injective] with $X=(L_qF)_n$, $Y=(F_q)_n$, $W=(\operatorname{colim}_I F)_n$: its injective map $f$ is the assumed latching map, while the map to $W$ may be arbitrary. It gives injectivity of $\operatorname{colim}_I F\to\operatorname{colim}_{I^+}F$ in every degree. The induction hypothesis for $I^+\subseteq H$ applies because $|H\setminus I^+|$ decreased by one, and composing these injections completes the finite induction. All latching objects used are those in $J$, since $H$ and each intermediate subset are downward closed in $J$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 6.4, printed p.12: pushout stability supplies the induction step, specialized to sets in each degree.

proof.text: Return to $J=\mathcal P_{<}(S)$ and $F=Z$. For $T\subsetneq S'$, the latching diagram for $A$ at $T$ is exactly $(Z_R)_{R\subsetneq T}$, so its latching map is the assumed one for $Z_T$. Thus $A$ is cofibrant. The map $a\to C$ is the latching map for the proper subset $S'\subsetneq S$, hence is degreewise injective as well.

source.place: Section 6.3 cofibrancy definition and Proposition 6.4, left vertical map, printed pp.11-12.

proof.text: For $T\subsetneq S'$ put $V=T\cup\{s\}$, a proper subset of $S$, and let $H_T=\mathcal P_{<}(V)$ and $D_T=H_T\setminus\{T\}$. Both are downward closed in $J$: $T$ is maximal in $H_T$, since $V$ adds only the element $s$ to $T$. Restricting cocones gives $\operatorname{colim}_{D_T}Z\cong\operatorname{colim}_{R\subsetneq T}Z_{R\cup\{s\}}$. To verify this directly, every object $U$ of $D_T$ not containing $s$ satisfies $U\subsetneq T$ and has the arrow $U\to U\cup\{s\}\in D_T$; extend a cocone on the containing objects using this arrow. For a cross-face inclusion $U\subseteq W$, the factorization through $U\cup\{s\}\subseteq W$ verifies compatibility. Restriction and extension are inverse. By steps 2-4 the map from this colimit to $\operatorname{colim}_{H_T}Z$ is degreewise injective. Composing with the assumed latching injection $\operatorname{colim}_{H_T}Z\to Z_V$ proves precisely that the latching map of $B$ at $T$ is injective. Thus $B$ is cofibrant; when $T=\varnothing$, $D_T$ and its containing subcategory are both empty, so the argument still applies.

source.place: Section 6.3 shifted face X′ and Proposition 6.4 induction, printed pp.11-12: shifted cofibrancy expanded using the proved downset induction.

proof.text: Let $D=\mathcal P_{<}(S)\setminus\{S'\}$ and $I=\{R:R\subsetneq S'\}$. These are downward closed in $J$, because $S'$ is maximal in $J$. The same explicit restriction-and-extension formula as in step 6 gives $\operatorname{colim}_D Z\cong b$: for $U\in D$ without $s$, use $U\to U\cup\{s\}$, which lies in the containing face indexed by $\mathcal P_{<}(S')$. Consequently the injective map $\operatorname{colim}_I Z\to\operatorname{colim}_D Z$ of steps 2-4 is the canonical map $a\to b$, since on every $Z_R$, $R\subsetneq S'$, it is the structure map $Z_R\to Z_{R\cup\{s\}}$ followed by its colimit map.

source.place: Section 6.3 natural map of face diagrams, printed p.11: monicity on face colimits via the same finite latching induction.

proof.text: In the pushout of step 1 use the already proved injection $a\to C$. For every degree, [lem-coef-set-pushout-injective] with $X=a_n$, $Y=C_n$, and $W=b_n$ proves that $b_n\to(C\amalg_a b)_n$ is injective. The comparison with $\operatorname{colim}Z$ of step 1 therefore proves degreewise injectivity of the required canonical map $b\to\operatorname{colim}Z$.

source.place: Proposition 6.4, right vertical map, printed p.12: cobase change of the latching injection.

proof.text: All comparison maps above are induced by the displayed structure cocones. For a natural transformation $Z\to\widetilde Z$, the two composites in the comparison square agree after precomposition with every $Z_U$: at a non-containing object both use the component into $\widetilde C$, and at a containing object both use the component into $\operatorname{colim}\widetilde B$. Colimit uniqueness makes the square commute, and also gives commutation with every simplicial operator when the constructions are formed degreewise. Thus the isomorphism and all canonical maps are natural in $Z$; the finite ordering chosen to prove injectivity defines no comparison map. If $|S|=1$, then $S'=\varnothing$, $a=b=\varnothing$, $C=Z_\varnothing$, and the pushout is $C\amalg_\varnothing\varnothing=C=\operatorname{colim}Z$; the two face cofibrancy conditions are vacuous and all three asserted maps with empty source are injective.

source.place: Proposition 6.4, naturality and finite-induction base case, printed p.12; explicit singleton and simplicial-operator checks.
